messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: High error rate detected on inference routing service (internal-prod-routing). 5xx rate > 8% over 1m. Paging oncall: @jorge. Severity: P2.

jorge: oncall here, looking. seeing a spike in compile-time errors from the routing agent, starting ~12:04 UTC. will attach logs.

alex: I can see the same from the metrics dashboard — route-compile backlog jumped and caused timeouts to the model pool, causing 502s upstream.

jorge: mitigation plan: 1) flip traffic to routing-fallback-policy-2026 (less aggressive compile path) 2) scale dedicated routing-workers by +25% (manual) 3) enable temporary circuit breaker for any route with >3 sequential compile failures. doing step 1 now.

jorge: done step 1 — traffic moved to fallback policy. errors dropping from 8% -> 1.6% (observed in 30s). continuing step 2.

lauren: thanks. keep CS looped — Maya will need numbers for customer impact.

maya: noted. Maria (Acct) asked what to tell the customer. we need window, % of requests affected, and actions + ETA for RCA. can you confirm impact numbers when you have them?

jorge: window is 12:03:45 UTC -> 12:10:20 UTC (failures spike). peak error rate ~8.4% across global prod, but for affected dedicated customers estimate ~12% of requests failed (routing paths that touched the compile backlog). total affected customers: 3 dedicated accounts experienced degraded requests, one saw a 6-minute tail. I'll export the logs and counts — uploading snippet below.

alex: logs (snip):
```
[12:04:01] routing-agent compile error: KernelSelectionTimeout: 60000ms
[12:04:12] upstream: 502 Bad Gateway (compile backlog)
[12:05:07] routing-agent: fallback policy active for route=customer-42
```

maya: thanks — draft customer note (suggested):

"Hi <Customer>,

We observed a transient routing-related degradation on <date> between 12:03–12:10 UTC which caused a subset of requests to fail with 5xx responses. During the peak, approximately 10–15% of requests from your dedicated fleet experienced failures; most requests were served successfully. We mitigated the issue by switching to a fallback routing policy and scaling routing workers, which restored normal service.

We are investigating the root cause and will follow up with an RCA and preventative actions within 48 hours. We apologize for the disruption and are available to discuss impact and remediation options (including service credit if desired).

Regards,
Redwood Support"

lauren: looks good. couple of notes: 1) don't promise a timeline longer than our SLA on RCAs — say "we will share a detailed RCA within 48 hours" is fine. 2) add link to status page entry and include contact for urgent follow-up.

sam: FYI from infra side — we pushed a change to the routing compilation circuit config in the early morning deploy (02:10 UTC). initial review suggests a config drift combined with an unlucky request distribution spike. putting together a root-cause hypothesis.

priya: proposed preventative actions to include in RCA: - stronger canary gating on routing compile config changes - alerting on compile-queue depth per-region with lower thresholds - automated fallback thresholds (so policy flips before customer-visible failures) - regression test for compile congestion under synthetic load.

maya: I'll update the customer draft to include the status page link and a line about our next steps (RCA + preventative list). also asking for a recommended credit amount — engineering, is there a measurable SLA breach?

lauren: check the SLA window: for dedicated customers, we track availability per-hour. Since degradation was under 10 minutes for most, it may not qualify for an automatic credit, but offer a discretionary goodwill credit if they request. Ops to confirm.

jorge: uploaded counts csv to the incident folder: affected_requests.csv — shows per-customer failed request counts. For customer-42: 1.2k requests in window, 140 failures (11.7%).

maya: updated draft with specifics and status page link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1746801234-routing. Final customer message below — please review:

"Hi <Customer>,

Summary: On <date> between 12:03–12:10 UTC we experienced a transient routing degradation that caused 11–13% of requests from your dedicated fleet to fail with 5xx responses. The issue was resolved by switching to a fallback routing policy and scaling routing workers.

Impact: Affected requests were concentrated on routing paths that hit a compile backlog. Three customers experienced brief degraded success rates; for your account specifically, 140 of ~1.2k requests failed during the window.

Remediation & Next Steps: We mitigated the incident within ~3 minutes by enabling the fallback policy and completed scaling within ~6 minutes. We will provide a full RCA within 48 hours including: root cause analysis, timelines, and the following preventative actions we plan to implement: stronger canary gating on routing compile config changes, region-level compile queue alerts, automated fallback thresholds, and a synthetic regression test for compile congestion.

If you prefer, we can schedule a quick 30-minute call to walk through the impact and next steps. We apologize for the disruption.

Best,
Redwood Inference Support Team"

sam: wording is clear. suggest adding a small technical appendix in the RCA about the compile kernel selection timeouts and the specific config keys changed.

priya: agree. also recommend we include a timeline in the customer note (concise): 12:03 detection, 12:04 fallback policy flip, 12:06 workers scaled, 12:10 all clear.

maya: added the timeline line. one more: ops — please confirm whether to proactively offer a credit or wait for customer request.

lauren: ops to review — we usually wait unless the account asks, offer discretionary credit if business impact was material. I'll loop finance if needed.

maya: final: I'll post to the customer now and update the status page with the timeline + RCA ETA. will ping here when done. :white_check_mark:

jorge: thanks team. filing follow-on ticket to add the automated fallback threshold and canary gating work items. linking to GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/4821

IncidentBot: RESOLVED: incident routing spike mitigated and fallback policy active. Incident closed at 12:10:20 UTC.

maya: customer message sent. customer asked to schedule a call tomorrow 15:00 UTC — setting up invite.

lauren: nice work — please include the transient logs and counts in the RCA doc. closing the loop here. :slightly_smiling_face:
